enquiry: Our research group is evaluating a spectral measurement interface using model biological tissues such as chicken muscle, fat and liver. We want to compare MIR ATR and fluorescence information, because the material is heterogeneous and sequential measurements may not sample the same location. This is a laboratory classification study. We need a first comparison experiment and a clear statement of what its results would demonstrate.

clarification_questions.question: What decision should the classification result support in the end: a tissue-identification tool for research, a clinical or surgical aid, or a process check in food or production?
clarification_questions.why: Defines whether a laboratory comparison is sufficient or whether the design must anticipate a later use case.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Laboratory research only; no clinical or industrial readiness is assumed, and the results are treated as a feasibility comparison.

clarification_questions.question: Which tissue classes must be distinguished (muscle, fat, liver only, or others), and is any specific analyte or indicator of interest defined within them?
clarification_questions.why: Sets the classification task and tells whether a fluorescent species or specific chemical marker is needed.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Classes are muscle, fat and liver as stated; no specific analyte is defined, so fluorescence targets must be justified in lab screening.

clarification_questions.question: Do the tissues contain a known fluorescent species or indicator, and if so which one?
clarification_questions.why: Fluorescence only measures a defined fluorescent species or a justified indicator; this decides whether fluorescence adds information.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Fluorescent species unknown; lab screening must establish whether any fluorescence signal exists before it is used for classification.

clarification_questions.question: In what physical state and optical appearance are the chicken samples measured (fresh or stored, cut surface, opaque, with fat and liquid exudate)?
clarification_questions.why: Determines contact quality with the ATR crystal and whether the fluorescence signal is distorted by scattering.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Solid tissue, opaque, with surface contact to the ATR crystal assumed; surface condition unknown.

clarification_questions.question: How do the tissue samples vary within a sample (texture, fat-muscle layering, moisture, temperature) and over time during the measurement?
clarification_questions.why: Heterogeneity and drift set how many spots and replicates are needed and whether same-spot measurement is required.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Heterogeneous at the scale of the measurement spot; variation level unknown, lab screening will quantify it.

clarification_questions.question: What measurement set-up is planned: a combi probe measuring the same spot, or separate ATR and fluorescence measurements, and which fibers and spectrometers are available?
clarification_questions.why: Decides whether the claim that sequential measurements miss the same location can be tested directly, and which fiber types are compatible with MIR.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Separate measurements assumed in the first design; fiber and instrument availability unknown, and MIR requires mid-IR fibers, not silica.

clarification_questions.question: What reference method defines the true tissue class for each sample, and how accurate is it?
clarification_questions.why: Without a ground truth the classification result cannot be judged and the comparison has no benchmark.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Reference class is the known tissue type of each sample as prepared; its accuracy is not defined.

clarification_questions.question: What performance criteria should the comparison meet (classification accuracy, number of classes, acceptable misclassification), and what is the target response time if any?
clarification_questions.why: Defines what the first experiment must demonstrate to be judged a success.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Criteria not defined; the experiment is designed to report classification results per method without a pass threshold.

flags_before_revision.detail: not_supported: The cited S04 p.4 does report that neither single technique fully separated the three classes while the concatenated IR+fluorescence PCA did; the claim's core is supported. However the page does not discuss retesting on new samples, so that remark is an extrapolation not stated on the cited pages. Fix: Keep the finding that single methods did not fully separate the classes while the fused PCA did, and attribute the retest remark to a general limitation rather than to the cited pages.

overstated: S04 p.2 states that alternating measurements cannot guarantee complete coincidence of spots, which supports the claim; but the phrase 'must come from the same small area' for inhomogeneous tissue is a requirement that S01 p.8 frames as crucial/high accuracy, and S04 p.2 says alternating measurements 'cannot be used in clinical surgery', which the claim omits. The claim is broadly supported. Fix: Phrase as: spectra should be collected from the same small area, since alternating probes cannot guarantee spot coincidence (S04 p.2; S01 p.8).

different_context: The S04 p.4 finding is from chicken fat tissue classification in a lab study with PCA; the claim presents it as showing separation via the ester carbonyl band, but the ester carbonyl attribution is on S04 p.3, not p.4, and the claim transfers a lab tissue result to the recommendation context without saying so. Fix: Cite S04 p.3 for the ester carbonyl band at about 1740 cm-1 and state that the fat discrimination result is from a lab chicken-tissue model study.

not_supported: S04 p.1 and p.4 do not state that tight tissue contact or mid-IR fiber requirements apply; S04 p.2 describes ATR suitability for liquid or soft samples with tight contact, and S01 p.8 mentions fiber probes, but the 'not silica' fiber requirement is not stated on the cited pages. Fix: Cite S04 p.2 for the tight-contact requirement for ATR with liquid or soft samples and S01 p.8 for fiber-optic probes, and remove the unsupported mid-IR-not-silica statement or source it to S02 p.6.

different_context: The quoted statement that fluorescence is well suited for liver recognition is a lab model-tissue result; the claim presents it without that context. Fix: State that in the lab chicken-tissue model study, fluorescence was well suited for recognizing liver tissue (S04 p.4).

not_supported: The cited set includes many table rows that do not state that usefulness requires a fluorescent component; the fluorescent-component requirement is stated on S04 p.2/p.3 and S01 p.12 context, and the selectivity rating for fluorimetry is 'low' only in S01 Table 1 rows r18 and r19, not as a general caveat drawn from S04 p.4. Fix: Cite S04 p.2 for the fluorescent-component requirement and S01 p.6 (Table 1 rows 'Fluorimetry', selectivity low) for the selectivity rating only.

different_context: The fused-data grouping result is from the lab chicken-tissue study on a small sample set, but the claim presents it as a general result without saying so. Fix: State that in the lab model-tissue study (three samples per tissue type), fused IR and fluorescence data gave three groups corresponding to tissue types (S04 p.4).

not_supported: S01 p.7 discusses synergy of combined methods in general but does not state that each method must be assessed on its own first or that the gain is a hypothesis to test. Fix: Cite S04 p.4 for the single-method results and S01 p.7 for the general synergy concept, and label the expected gain as a hypothesis for AFS to test.

not_supported: S01 p.6 Table 1 lists ATR and fluorimetric probes as separate techniques, and S04 p.2 says alternating probes cannot guarantee coincidence; neither page states that a combi ATR/fluorescence probe is preferred. The recommendation is an inference not directly stated. Fix: Cite S04 p.2 for the spot-coincidence problem and S01 p.8 for the availability of multispectral probes, and present the combi-probe preference as an AFS recommendation rather than a sourced claim.

not_supported: S02 p.6 gives transmission ranges: UV-VIS silica 190-1200 nm, VIS-NIR silica 350-2400 nm, polycrystalline IR 3000 nm-17 um. The claim's 'partial (3-17 um)' coverage is consistent, but 'FLUO: UV-Vis silica covers the nominal range' and 'no coverage' for Vis-NIR silica in the MIR range are not stated on S01 p.12 or S01 p.9, which do not discuss fiber transmission. Fix: Base the rule check only on S02 p.6 transmission ranges and cite it alone; remove S01 p.12 and S01 p.9 as sources for fiber coverage.

not_supported: S04 p.3 does attribute low reproducibility of fat samples to higher inhomogeneity of the tissue type, which supports the claim; however the claim omits that this was in the reference study only. The statement is supported. Fix: No change required beyond keeping the reference-study context.

overstated: S01 p.7 says synergy may solve problems that single methods cannot handle or only partially; it does not state that fusion may fail to beat the best single method. The risk is an inference, presented as if drawn from the page. Fix: Cite S04 p.4 where fused data outperformed single methods in the lab study, and frame the risk as a possibility to verify rather than a finding of S01 p.7.

overstated: S04 p.4 reports only lab classification of chicken tissue, and the page does state the probe's broader potential applications; the claim's statement that results demonstrate lab separability of model tissues only is a fair reading, but 'not clinical or industrial use' is stated as a conclusion the page does not make. Fix: State that the results are from a lab model-tissue study (S04 p.4) and that clinical or industrial use was not tested.

rule_hints: nominal_range_not_instrument_range: A nominal method range is not the usable range of a specific instrument, fiber or probe. [guidance]

fiber_limits_wavelength: The fiber determines which wavelengths reach the probe. Silica fibers transmit up to about 2.4 um and cannot carry mid-IR; mid-IR needs chalcogenide, polycrystalline or hollow-waveguide fibers. [S02 p.6; S04 p.1]
remote_measurement_nir_silica: NIR works with standard glass optics and silica fibers, which suits remote online measurement; robust silica cables of 100-300 m exist. [S01 p.5; S02 p.7]
same_spot_for_heterogeneous: For heterogeneous or fast-changing samples, methods should measure the same spot at the same time, e.g. with a combi probe. [S01 p.8; S04 p.2]
do_not_invent: Do not invent measured results, accuracy, detection limits, response times, fiber lengths, product codes or prices, client facts, or guarantees. [guidance]
